principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status + #5 Error prevention
location: Recipe editor `/recipes/:id` — ColorPicker side panel, 'Use this colour' button (#47D1D1 cyan from wheel)
problem: Clicking 'Use this colour' on the wheel-picked custom hex appears to do nothing — the dialog closes, but the recipe still shows COLOR SLOTS · 0 and an empty + ADD COLOR tile. The user's selection is silently dropped. Verified twice; only paint-library clicks persist as slots. This is the headline Phase-12 flow and the first action a brand-new user is told to take ('Click a + box to start a recipe').
fix: In the colour-picker drawer (likely `app/src/components/recipes/ColorPickerDrawer.tsx` or equivalent), wire the wheel 'Use this colour' button to call the same `addSlot({ hex, source: 'custom' })` action that the library list uses. After mutation, close the drawer and animate the new slot in. Verify with a Playwright test that picks cyan, clicks Use, and asserts a Slot · 1 chip appears.

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency and standards + #2 Match between system and real world
location: Recipe editor side panel — `EDIT SLOT · SLOT 1` mode (slot is already filled)
problem: The instruction text says 'Click a filled slot to swap its paint.' But once the panel is open in EDIT SLOT mode, clicking a paint in the LIBRARY list does NOT replace the slot's paint — it APPENDS a new step to the Steps list. So the same click target (a library row) has two completely different meanings depending on entry path, and neither matches the stated 'swap' intent. The slot's swatch colour and the Steps' paint name end up disjoint.
fix: Disambiguate: in EDIT SLOT mode the primary action on a library click should be REPLACE the slot's paint, not append a step. Add a secondary 'Add as new step' action via a button in each library row (or move the 'add step' affordance into the Steps panel below). At minimum, label the panel's two modes ('Replace paint' vs 'Add new step') so the user sees which one is active.

principle: NN/g #4 + #2 (Layering ≠ /gradient)
location: `/tools` index card 'Layering' links to `/tools/gradient`; visiting `/tools/layering` returns the 404 page
problem: The Phase-12 Gradient → Layering rename only shipped on the UI label. The card on the Tools index page still hrefs `/tools/gradient`, and the wishlist Tools-dropdown sends users to `/tools/layering` which 404s. So one of the two navigation paths to Layering is broken.
fix: Pick one canonical route. Recommended: rename folder `app/src/app/tools/gradient/` → `app/src/app/tools/layering/` and update `app/src/components/tools/ToolCard.tsx` (or wherever the index card hrefs live). Add a redirect from `/tools/gradient` → `/tools/layering` in `next.config.ts` to preserve any bookmarked links. Search for `gradient` in the route tree to make sure nothing else still uses the old path.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and real world; Jakob's Law (deep links should respect the param)
location: Wishlist row 'Tools ▾' dropdown — 'Wheel' option, target `/tools/wheel?name=...`
problem: Clicking 'Wheel' on a wishlist paint row navigates to `/tools/wheel?name=Citadel+Combat+Patrol+—+Space+Marines` but the wheel page ignores the query and shows whatever palette state was already cached. The deep-link contract is broken: the user expected the picked paint to land in the wheel.
fix: In `app/src/app/tools/wheel/page.tsx` (or its client component), read `searchParams.name` (or use a `hex` param) and pre-seed the wheel palette with that paint's hex. Same fix needed for Match and Layering entry points from wishlist. Also: Tools-dropdown should pass `hex=` (deterministic) not `name=` (which requires a name → paint lookup).

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (3:1 minimum for UI components)
location: User page → Change Password card — three `<input type=password>` fields
problem: Password input borders measure `rgb(38,38,38)` on `rgb(10,10,10)` body bg = 1.4:1 contrast ratio. Below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor for UI components. Inputs look like flat black rectangles — not obviously inputs until clicked. Same pattern likely applies to every other form field in the app.
fix: Lift input borders to at least `--color-border-subtle` (~`#404040`, ~3.2:1) and add a 1px outline on `:focus-visible` in `--color-cyan`. Centralise in `globals.css` under a `.input-field` token. Also add associated `<label>` elements (currently labels are display-only text above each input — they're not programmatically linked).

principle: Phase-12 button discipline — cyan banished from buttons
location: App-wide: 'ATTACH RECIPE' (project detail), 'ASSIGN TO PROJECT ▾' (recipe editor), 'ASSIGN ▾' (recipes index + match results), '+ ADD NAMED MODEL' (project detail), 'CHANGE' / 'CHANGE PASSWORD' / 'SAVE FILTER' (user page), 'USE CAMERA' (eyedropper), 'FIND IN LIBRARY' (wheel), 'SEND TO RECIPE' (tools footer)
problem: Phase-12 cleanup said cyan was banished from buttons. Counted 10+ cyan-on-cyan-tint buttons surviving. They all read as 'tappable link' due to the cyan colour also being used for breadcrumb and title text — same colour, different meaning, two different affordances. Von Restorff effect is lost: cyan no longer signals 'primary action' because everything important is cyan.
fix: Decide button hierarchy: green = primary destructive-success (Save, Add, Create), yellow = secondary (Share, Export), red-outline = destructive (Delete, Sign Out), white-outline = tertiary. Apply across every button audit point above. Cyan should ONLY be used for clickable hyperlink text and headings. Centralise in a `<Button variant=...>` primitive.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and real world; Polaris empty-state guidance
location: `/recipes` index — 6 of 8 recipes named 'Untitled recipe' after a fresh user clicks NEW RECIPE
problem: Clicking NEW RECIPE creates a new recipe with name 'Untitled recipe' and drops the user into the editor — no name prompt. After 3 sessions the user has 6 indistinguishable rows in the recipes table. The recipes list becomes unusable as a navigation surface.
fix: Either (a) prompt for a name in a modal on NEW RECIPE click ('What's this scheme for?' with a single text input), or (b) auto-name from context ('Untitled · Citadel Combat Patrol scheme') and append a sequence number when ambiguous, or (c) leave Untitled but show a one-time banner in the editor: 'Give this recipe a name (click the title).' Recommend (a) for clarity.

principle: NN/g #1 + Refactoring UI 'design with real content'
location: Project detail page `/projects/:id` — H1 title 'Audit Round 4 Test'
problem: On the recipe editor the H1 is contenteditable + click-to-edit, but on the project detail page the same-looking H1 is NOT editable. Click does nothing, no rename affordance, no edit pencil. Inconsistent inline-edit behaviour across two near-identical surfaces — recruits will try and silently fail.
fix: Either make the project H1 contenteditable to match (apply the same `<EditableTitle>` component used on recipes — likely `app/src/components/EditableTitle.tsx` after extraction), or add an explicit 'Rename' menu item to a project header overflow menu. Recommend matching the recipe editor pattern for consistency.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.4.5 Multiple ways + Jakob's Law (mobile nav parity)
location: Mobile (375×812) bottom nav — only 5 items: Projects / Library / Recipes / Tools / Wishlist. User tab is gone.
problem: On mobile there is no way to reach `/user`. The desktop sidebar's User entry is hidden, and the mobile profile pill in the top-right (the 'T ON' button) does not navigate. Users can't change their password, set recovery email, edit brand filter, export data, or sign out from a phone.
fix: Two options: (a) make the top-right avatar pill in `MobileHeader.tsx` an actual link to `/user`; or (b) extend the bottom nav to 6 items by adding User (acceptable up to ~6 per Miller's Law). Recommend (a) — keeps bottom nav tight and matches Jakob's Law (avatar-in-corner-goes-to-account-page is the dominant pattern).

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency + Hick's Law (clean up choices)
location: Wishlist row 'Tools ▾' dropdown — only shows Wheel / Match / Layering
problem: The Wishlist Tools dropdown lists 3 of the 4 tools — Image Eyedropper is missing. Likely correct that Eyedropper doesn't accept a single paint (it takes an image), but the omission is unexplained. Also: the dropdown is named 'TOOLS' — same word as the sidebar nav and the page header — which conflates page-level navigation with a per-row action. Recruits will mis-target.
fix: Rename the per-row dropdown from 'TOOLS ▾' to 'USE WITH ▾' or 'OPEN IN ▾' so it doesn't collide with the Tools page name. Keep the 3 tools that accept a single colour input. If Eyedropper takes images, omit it (correct behaviour) — no comment needed once the rename clarifies the intent.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — 24 CSS px minimum, recommended 44px
location: Project dashboard `/projects` — disclosure caret `▸` on parent rows (e.g., 'Test Grey Knights')
problem: Caret button measures 20×20 px (verified via getBoundingClientRect). Below the WCAG 2.2 24px floor and well below the 44×44 HIG/Material recommendation. Also: the caret does NOT rotate from `▸` to `▾` on expand, so the only feedback that 'this row is expanded' is the indentation of the now-visible children.
fix: Increase hit-target to at least 36×36 (a 16px caret with 10px padding). Rotate the caret (CSS `transform: rotate(90deg)` with a 150ms transition) on expand. Add `aria-expanded='true|false'` to the button. Source: `app/src/components/dashboard/*` or `ProjectTree.tsx`.

principle: Refactoring UI typography; Apple HIG minimum 11pt; WCAG zoom resilience
location: App-wide chrome — top status bar `SYS · OK · NET · ON · TIME`, table headers `NAME / TYPE / RECIPES`, badge labels `WISHLIST / PURCHASED`, footer `// STABLE`, 'no recipes', 'Medium', completion '0%'
problem: 59 distinct text nodes render at ≤11px. 11px is the Apple HIG minimum FONT POINT, and on the web Refactoring UI recommends 14–16px body. The terminal aesthetic intent is fine but 11px x IBM Plex Sans (proportional, not monospace) leaves recruits squinting. 11px text-secondary plus opacity:0.5 ('no recipes', 'Medium') compounds.
fix: Bump global type scale: chrome/status bar 12px, table headers 12px (uppercase, +0.5 letter-spacing), body 14px, status badges 12px. Audit `globals.css` for any `text-[11px]` or `text-xs` (Tailwind = 12px) Tailwind uses and replace with named tokens (`--text-chrome: 12px`, `--text-body: 14px`). Keep aesthetic.

principle: Universal — consistency over cleverness; Polaris semantic colour
location: Library page `/library` — top-right decorative '02' at 96px font, color `rgba(125,211,252,0.1)`
problem: Big '02' decoration top-right — measured 96px × 106px, 1.06:1 contrast against the page bg, no semantic meaning visible to a recruit. Could be a page number, a brand mark, or chrome residue from an earlier iteration. Either way it competes with the FILTERS button for attention without communicating anything.
fix: If it's chrome decoration for the terminal aesthetic, keep but reduce to 32px and move out of the FILTERS button's visual proximity (corner of the page chrome, not floating over content). If it's a leftover, delete it. Search for the literal `02` in `app/src/app/library/` and `app/src/components/library/`.

principle: Doherty Threshold (400ms); NN/g #1 Visibility of system status
location: Page scroll on long pages (User page especially) — fixed top status bar leaves a visible flash of unstyled / empty area before content settles
screenshot: ss_3919h5tq4 (first frame in the scroll batch)
problem: While scrolling the User page, an interim frame showed an empty black viewport with the status bar reattaching at y≈445. Visible layout shift, no skeleton, no progressive reveal. Most likely the fixed status bar is recalculating its position. On a phone with intermittent network this would feel broken.
fix: Lock the top status bar via `position: sticky; top: 0` with a fixed height in `globals.css`. Ensure the document body has matching `padding-top` so content never slides under it. Test with throttled CPU in DevTools to confirm no jank.

principle: NN/g #4; Aesthetic-Usability — first impressions of the recipe editor
location: Recipe editor — action buttons cluster top-right: SAVE TO LIBRARY (green) / ASSIGN TO PROJECT ▾ (cyan) / SHARE RECIPE (white outline) / DELETE (red outline)
problem: Four buttons, four visual treatments — no clear primary. SAVE is green but the recipe IS auto-saving ('saved' indicator in NOTES panel). ASSIGN is cyan — competes with SAVE. SHARE is plain. DELETE is destructive. The user can't tell which one is the 'finish this' button.
fix: If the recipe auto-saves, drop the SAVE TO LIBRARY button entirely (replace with the 'saved · just now' indicator). Make ASSIGN TO PROJECT the only primary action (green). Move SHARE + DELETE into an overflow `⋯` menu. Net: one green primary, one overflow menu.

principle: NN/g #2 + Refactoring UI 'labels are values'
location: Library detail panel — chip labels `o PAINT` and `· MEDIUM CONFIDENCE`
problem: The `o` prefix on `PAINT` (type icon legend) is opaque to a first-time user. `MEDIUM CONFIDENCE` is undocumented — confidence in what? The hex extraction? Why is this surfaced to the end-user at all?
fix: Either hide the data-quality fields (CONFIDENCE) on the user-facing panel — they're internal metadata. Replace `o PAINT` with a proper icon + the word 'Paint' OR drop the redundant duplication. Add a `<TypeLegend>` tooltip on hover so the symbol legend is discoverable.

principle: Carbon — domain consistency + brand integrity
location: Library detail panel — `SOURCE: https://www.minimatch.app/paint/...`
problem: Each paint detail panel exposes a `SOURCE` link pointing to https://www.minimatch.app — a different paint-tracking product. Attribution is fine in principle, but presenting a competitor's URL prominently on every paint detail will (a) drive recruits to evaluate a competitor mid-task, and (b) read like an embarrassing accidental leak. If this is intentional attribution, it should at least be a small footer caption, not a 14px link.
fix: Move SOURCE to a small 11px caption near the bottom of the panel ('Catalogue source: minimatch.app') OR remove from the user-facing panel and surface only on an internal admin view. If keeping for transparency, label as 'Catalogue attribution' so the intent is clear.

principle: NN/g #1 + Apple HIG (close-the-loop on dropdowns)
location: Tools index page `/tools` — `← TOOLS` back-arrow button at top-left
problem: On the Tools INDEX page, the `← TOOLS` chip is visible top-left. Clicking it does nothing (we're already at /tools). It's only meaningful on inner tool pages (`/tools/wheel`, `/tools/match`, etc). Dead UI on the parent page.
fix: Hide the back-chip on the Tools index page (conditional render based on `usePathname()` !== '/tools'). Source: `app/src/components/tools/ToolShell.tsx` or wherever the chip lives.

principle: Phase-12 — per-tool 'Assign ▾' parity (R7-4 follow-through)
location: Colour Wheel `/tools/wheel`, Layering `/tools/gradient`, Eyedropper `/tools/eyedropper` — per-swatch row actions
problem: The Cross-brand Match page has `USE` + `ASSIGN ▾` on every result row — great. The other three tools only have a single bottom-right `SEND TO RECIPE` button that ships the whole palette. There is no per-swatch / per-step assign in Wheel, Layering, or Eyedropper. Inconsistent. Recruits will look for the same affordance.
fix: Add a per-row `ASSIGN ▾` button to: every swatch in `/tools/wheel` (already has `FIND IN LIBRARY` — add ASSIGN next to it), every step in `/tools/gradient` ramp, every extracted dominant colour in `/tools/eyedropper`. The dropdown opens 'Assign to recipe slot' picker. Reuse the Match page's component.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.4.10 Reflow; Refactoring UI 'design with real content'
location: Mobile (375×812) Projects table — columns NAME / TYPE / RECIPES / STATUS / PRIORITY / COMPLETION
problem: On mobile the dashboard table renders horizontally with each cell visible but project names wrap mid-word ('Audit Round 4 Test' breaks into three lines because the name column is squeezed). The COMPLETION column scrolls off-screen — the user must side-scroll to see progress.
fix: On viewport <768px, transform the table into a stacked card list: each project becomes a card with name (top), type+status badge row (middle), and a percentage bar at the bottom. Hide PRIORITY behind a long-press / kebab menu. Source: `app/src/components/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx` + add a `useMediaQuery` switch.

principle: NN/g #2 + Polaris empty-state guidance
location: Project detail Color Scheme box — three empty `+` boxes
problem: Instruction text says 'Click a + box to start a recipe for this project — the boxes fill in with the picked paints.' But clicking the FIRST `+` did nothing (silent failure) until I tried the second. May be a state-loading race, or the first box may be disabled until certain conditions are met. Either way: no feedback. Also: why three boxes? What do they mean? Recruits will assume the 3 slots correspond to base/midtone/highlight but there's no labelling.
fix: Audit click handlers on the empty 3-box scaffold. If only the 'first unfilled' box should respond, disable the others visually (greyed + non-pointer). Add a tiny caption under each box: 'Slot 1' / 'Slot 2' / 'Slot 3'. Better yet: a single 'Start a recipe' CTA that creates the recipe + opens the slot picker, no scaffolding boxes needed.

principle: NN/g #3 User control and freedom
location: Project detail — auto-creates a recipe named 'Audit Round 4 Test scheme' the instant a + box is clicked
problem: Clicking the second + box created a fully-named recipe (`Audit Round 4 Test scheme`) auto-attached to the project. No confirmation. No name prompt. No undo. The user wasn't told that 'click + box' means 'commit to a permanent recipe with this exact name'. If the user meant to just preview options, the recipes list is now polluted.
fix: Either (a) keep the auto-create but add an inline 'undo' toast for 5 s ('Recipe created — undo?'), or (b) require an explicit confirmation modal on first slot creation. Same fix as #007 — let the user name the thing. Bonus: surface the auto-name pattern ('AppendScheme') somewhere in the empty-state copy so users aren't surprised.

principle: Apple HIG — no surprises on layout; reduce content shift
location: User page on mobile/desktop — first scroll frame shows blank top half before content settles
problem: During a fast downscroll on the User page, a frame showed a black void above the CHANGE PASSWORD card (the status bar repositioning, presumably). Looks like a layout-shift on resize/scroll. Pretty rare in practice but the visual indicates that the top status bar / chrome isn't reserving space correctly.
fix: Inspect `app/src/app/layout.tsx` and any fixed/sticky positioning on the status bar. Ensure the `<main>` element has `padding-top: var(--chrome-height)` and that the chrome is sized predictably. Add a `min-height: 100dvh` to the layout container.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 Info and Relationships
location: App-wide form inputs — password inputs on /user, recipe-name editing on /recipes/:id, hex input on /tools/match
problem: Visible label text ('CURRENT PASSWORD') sits in a sibling element but is not programmatically associated with the input — `aria-label` empty, `closest('label')` empty. Screen readers will announce the input as 'edit text' with no purpose.
fix: Wrap each input in `

principle: NN/g #4 Consistency + Carbon — token naming hygiene
location: Internal vs display naming — `/tools/gradient` route URL still says 'gradient' but UI says 'Layering'; Wishlist row STATUS badge says 'WISHLIST' but the page title is 'WISHLIST' (so a wishlist row says 'this is on the wishlist' — tautological)
problem: Multiple lingering naming inconsistencies post-Phase 12: (a) URL `gradient` vs UI 'Layering' (covered in #003); (b) wishlist STATUS column says 'WISHLIST' on the wishlist page — redundant. (c) Project type chip says 'UNIT' but the parent project type is also 'UNIT' — chip is data-redundant with the parent badge.
fix: (a) is fixed by #003. (b) on the wishlist page, hide the 'WISHLIST' status badge — show only when the status is NOT wishlist (e.g., 'PURCHASED', 'HOLD'). (c) Drop the per-row TYPE chip when the parent is the same type; show it only when there's a type mismatch (Army with a Unit child = show; Army with only Army children = hide).

principle: NN/g #1 Visibility of system status
location: Top status bar `SYS · OK · NET · LAG / ON · TIME · 04:01:09`
problem: The top chrome shows 'NET · LAG' sometimes and 'NET · ON' other times. Recruits won't know what LAG means (network latency? Connection degraded?). No tooltip, no explanation, no action affordance. If it's a state worth surfacing, give the user something they can do about it. If it's noise, hide it.
fix: Either expand on hover ('Network response slower than 500ms — your edits may take a moment to save') with a 'Retry' action if applicable, or drop the LAG variant and only show ON / OFF / OFFLINE. The terminal aesthetic is great but state has to be actionable.

principle: WCAG 2.2 §1.3.1 + landmark hygiene
location: App-wide DOM — 8 `<header>` elements, 4 `<nav>` elements, 0 `<footer>`
problem: DOM has 8 `<header>` landmarks (probably card-section headings using the wrong element) and 4 `<nav>` landmarks. Screen reader users navigating by landmark get a confusing audit list. Recommended: 1 banner header, 1 main nav, 1 main content, 1 footer.
fix: Audit places where `<header>` is used inside cards/panels (e.g., 'COLOR SCHEME', 'ROSTER', 'RECIPE · 1'). Replace with `<h2>` or `<div role='heading' aria-level='2'>`. The mobile bottom-tab-bar and the desktop sidebar-rail should both be `<nav>` — but the top status bar should be `<header role='banner'>`, not another `<nav>`.

principle: Phase-12 — decorative `[ ]` bracket removal from chrome
location: Projects page `/projects` — search hint `[ / ]` next to the empty input, also similar bracket-chip in some chrome
problem: The `[ / ]` shortcut hint floats next to the QuickAdd input. Looks like keyboard-shortcut chrome (Press / to focus search), but reads as decorative chrome to a recruit. Brackets-as-decoration was on the R7 cleanup list.
fix: Either show this as a proper kbd hint inside the input ('Press / to focus' as placeholder) or drop the floating bracket chip. Verify nothing else uses `[ ... ]` decorative wrappers on top-level chrome.

principle: NN/g #2 Match between system and real world
location: Wishlist page — 'Citadel Combat Patrol — Space Marines' is in the PAINTS table
problem: A Citadel Combat Patrol kit is a model box, not a paint. But it's been sorted into the PAINTS section of the wishlist, while MODELS · 0 is empty. The auto-routing (vendor URL → category) made the wrong call. Recruits will assume the routing is broken (it is, here).
fix: Audit the vendor-URL → category heuristic in `app/src/lib/scrape/...`. 'Combat Patrol' is a Games Workshop product line that's always a model box. Whitelist that phrase. Add a manual 'Move to Models' affordance per row in case the heuristic mis-routes.

principle: Doherty Threshold; perceived performance
location: Recipe editor ColorPicker drawer — Library list 'Show closer matches'
problem: Library shows '50 matches' for any color, including pure cyan #47D1D1 — but the first 10 visible matches are 'Medium Grey', 'Pale Blue', 'Ocean Blue' — NOT cyan. The matches are clearly not sorted by similarity to the picked colour. 'Show closer matches' implies the user must manually request relevance — but a relevance sort should be the default.
fix: Sort library matches by deltaE distance to the picked colour by default. Drop the 'Show closer matches' button or rename it to 'Show fewer · top 10' so the user can narrow the list. The current behaviour (50 unsorted) makes the wheel→library bridge feel broken.
